comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
Ok dude...here is a lot of feedback. I played the whole game on medium one shot without dying once and finished the whole game in 24 minutes. 

1) game run great! It's very smooth. Graphics look polished. This is a pro...   
2) game is too easy. By about level 6 my ship was so OP that I killed every enemy without even having to really move.   
3) different weapons are definitely cool. Controls are bit too sensitive like ship needs to move a little bit slower.   
4) boss battles are a bit too generic. Each boss should be unique. Different destructible parts was a good addition but it needs to be even more extreme like blowing off whole sections of boss piece by piece.   
5) music is pretty good and good enough. Sounds mixing is poor. The audio effects (like missle file, lasers and explosions) need to be louder or the music softer.   
6) It was difficult for me to see certain enemy bullets when they were blue.   
7) game is over all very solid but poor replayability because there just isn't anything new to see stage to stage. 

Suggestions: 

1) first suggestion is make you stages look different with different themes. This shouldn't be hard to implement. Make some fighting in space, some fighting on different looking planets, some fighting flying along the surface of huge capital ships.   
2) Add world building and some type of story. Stages should progress as if completing missions in places in the galaxy.  Add a screen with a little mission briefing between stages, give each location a name.   
3) Add a character like a cute anime girl that's the pilot on top corner. She gets excited when she completes a mission and looks distressed when the shields go down. It just needs to be a little head of the pilot type of thing. A game that did this was "U.N. Squadron".   
4) To add difficulty and variety, make it so when the shit gets hit after losing shield, weapons are downgraded.   
5) Like "Raiden" you could have variable power ups the switch weapon systems or upgrade the existing on if you pick it up at the right time.   
6) if you really want to add world building you could have different enemy types with different themed levels but this would be more work than simply adding level themes.   
7) You could add different plane tops and character selections like "Aero Fighters".   
8) "U.N. Squadron" also had a weapons arms seller character between missions when purchased upgrades".   
9) You could make the pilot a male character and then have a female hander or dispatcher that occasionally pops up to give orders or feedback. She should be cute. Think "Shifty" from Nikke: Goddess of Victory. 

As a general rule you want each stage to look different and show the player something new. This incentivizes them to keep playing because they want to see what the next stage looks like. If you have some simple story they also want to playout the story to see the full story. 

https://preview.redd.it/r8c081unj4th1.png?width=702&format=png&auto=webp&s=c590b889204db428e85670f912ed6e7c0a6a7e8e

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
OK I played it again. It's better with changes. Level 2 background theme change was refreshing.   


Seekers are my favorite but they are too OP. They clear the screen the whole time. 

You want each level to have a completely different aesthetic and theme. Here are some ideas.   
  
1) A water planet   
2) A desert planet   
3) asteroid belt with occasionally large asteroid you have to dodge or smash up.   
4) jungle planet.   
5) surface of giant capital ship (think x-wings flying over Death Star surface.    
6) moon surface like with craters   
7) prehistoric planet   
8) volcano planet with rivers of lava and volcanoes.   
9) across the rings of saturn   
10) inside a giant gas giant   
11) outer space 

You get the idea. radically different, each with a completely different theme and color scheme. 

Now you if you really want to level this up.... This is game play from the video game Raiden. 

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KeajSN7g9ro](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KeajSN7g9ro) 

You are flying across the surface but there are two types of enemies. You have flying enemies and you have ground enemies like building, tanks, ships on water, etc. 

Now each level is actually a level instead of just a background design. 

I realize doing something like that add a lot of extra work, but that's what made these old video games so interesting to play. There was constantly something new to see. There was actually level design. In Raiden you vertically scrolling but there are like sub-boss area where you stop scrolling and have to eliminate different enemies before the scrolling continues. 

Ok so now a water planet has ships you have fly by and shoot. Space levels would fly by space stations. Planets would have ground turret defences that scroll down, etc. 

Now each level you are trying to put the player into another world and spark their imagination constantly showing them something interesting. 

The game "Metal Slug" is done this way. 

\--

Other thoughts, 

Most of the other suggestions I gave you would make the game more interesting like having a dispatcher and pilot head that's expressing emotion, a story, etc. 

You can easily use a text-2-speech model to generate some actual dialog for the pilot of dispatcher. 

But here is another idea that I think would make the game play much more interested. 

One way to do this is to create .wav files for different events. 

Say your shields are reduced to zero. the program simply rolls one of 20 different possible voices events for no shields. Just use an LLM to come up with the different voice events. Then use a speech to text model to generate the dialog. Then upload the .wav files to Claude and it get it right the code to trigger one of 20 randomly. 

* "Shields depleted, Commander!"
* "Barrier collapsed. Watch your six!"
* "Deflectors are down, Captain!"
* "Shields at zero! Take evasive action!"
* "Energy barrier lost. We are exposed!"
* "Shield matrix is offline!"
* "Hull integrity exposed, sir!"
* "Shield grid collapsed. Recharging now!"
* "Defensive grid is burned out!"
* "Warning: Structural shields at zero percent!"
* "We're wide open! Watch out!"
* "Shields gone! Get us out of here!"
* "They broke through our barriers!"
* "Direct hits incoming! Shields are down!"
* "No shields! Brace for impact!"
* Shields down. Initiating backup protocols."
* "Deflectors lost. Awaiting your command."
* "Barrier neutralized. Readying armor plating."
* "Shields offline. Focus on firepower."
* "Energy grid failed. Hull taking the load."

Random voice even that triggers when defeating a powerful enemy. 

* "Target neutralized! Spectacular shot, Captain!"
* "They're down! That was incredible, sir!"
* "Direct hit! Massive explosion confirmed!"
* "Scratch one giant! You actually did it!"
* "Boom! Now *that* is how it's done!"
* "Threat eliminated! I can't believe we survived that!"
* "Enemy destroyed! Whew... my sensors were redlining."
* "They're gone! Great job, Commander—we made it!"
* "Target broken! I knew you could pull it off!"
* "Hostile down! Unbelievable flying out there!"
* "Target confirmed destroyed! Excellent tactical execution!"
* "Threat neutralized! Perfection, Captain!"
* "Anomalous signature eliminated! Threat level is zero."
* "Enemy flagship broken! Combat data looks flawless."
* "Hostile completely wiped. Stellar performance, sir!"
* "Target smoked! They didn't stand a chance against you."
* "Down for the count! Who's next?"
* "And *stay* down! Beautiful work, Commander!"
* "Enemy eliminated! Remind me never to get on your bad side."
* "They're history! You made that look easy!"

You can have a random voice even trigger for; 

Powerups   
defeating mini-boss.   
Completing level   
shield down   
high combo achievements   
Low heath   
Mission briefing   
boss fight engagements   
etc. 

\-- 

Now this is where you add charm to the game. The voice events can be from a copilot/navigator or a dispatcher or the onboard computer system like R2D2 in Star Wars. 

You have a cute anime girl that is very emotive and expressive.   
Positive events triggers like defeating a boss, have a happy voice event to validate the player.  
losing shields has a worried emotion. "be careful!"   
los health and the copilot is panicking and freaking out!   
Extra powerups and the copilot is super excited. "We're going to kick their asses now, sir!" "Weapons at full power, Lets kill them all!" 

So you put your cute anime copilot on thumbnail at the top of the UI then you trigger emotional voice events. I am actually pretty sure the original "Star Fox" game did this. 

But you have added an emotional arch in to the game that ebbs and flows from distress to excite to achievement and this will really add immersion into the game. 

\-- 

You could make ship weapons powerups temporary. Then you place powerups at increments during the level. 

At some points, powerups would stack and you ship would be OP but they each run out on their own timer. 

So you ship is constantly getting more power and less power during the game. It create sort of a rhythm as you play. Player will have to focus to survive when power ups aren't active but then will get really excited when they can manage to stack three for a bit and get OP. 

Then you have periods where the game is too easy and periods where it difficult. Now getting those powerups is actually more important. 

Now your ship power is constantly in a state of getting a little more powerful or little less powerful as you go. 

This would make the gameplay much more interesting. 

\--

Having large final boss with destructible parts that actually fly was a good idea too.   
You want each boss fight to be unique and interesting.   
  
Maybe you have to remove several layers of armor before you can actually damage the core of the enemy and reduce it's health. 

Maybe you have remove several weapons to make it easier to survive.   
  
There is a boss fight at 7:18 on Raiden.   
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KeajSN7g9ro](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KeajSN7g9ro)   
  
What how the boss fight progressing in stages with different challenges during each phase.

replies.author: Competitive_Might709
replies.body:
Thanks for coming back and playing again. Hearing that the level 2 change made a difference is really useful, and I appreciate how much detail you’ve put into this.

Your point about actual level design is the biggest takeaway for me. A water planet should have ships and defenses that change how you play, not just a different image underneath the same enemies. That gives me a much clearer direction for the next update.

I’ve added this to the plan: more distinct environments and encounters, ground and air targets, boss phases where destroying a part changes the fight, and character reactions that bring the story into the gameplay.

The temporary power-ups idea also fits really well with an attack-fusion bonus I’ve been thinking about. Those short moments where everything stacks could feel great, as long as surviving without them is still fun.

And thanks for flagging Seekers again. I want to keep what makes them your favorite while making sure they don’t play the whole game for you.

There’s a lot here, so I’d rather get one level working really well in this direction before spreading it across the game. This kind of feedback genuinely helps me figure out what to build next.

replies.author: Jolly-Rip5973
replies.body:
Cool. I realize the voice event thing would be a lot of work but damn it would be so freaking cool man! 

It would add an emotional depth to the game play that would take the person on an interesting emotional roller-coaster. It would be so much more engaging. 

If you added an emotional story arch on top of that you could actually sell you game on steam. 

The 90s video game U.N. Squadron took about 30 minutes to complete. 

There was a SNES version that had 1.5 hours to 3.5 hour campaign to complete the game. 

\-- 

But that type of thing is really extra polish that makes the game really high quality. 

The level design aspects would take priority.
